newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish customs find radioactive crucifix on train.
newsitem.headline: Polish customs find radioactive crucifix on train.

text.p: Polish border guards halted a train from Moscow on Monday after it set off a radiation detector, and found the source was a crucifix hidden by smugglers in a carriage roof, officials said.

"The origin of the radiation turned out to be a metal crucifix more than a metre long hidden under the roof, along with several icons," Miroslaw Szacillo, an official at the border guards' headquarters, told public television news.

"The wagon will be sealed because its seats are still showing some traces of contamination," Szacillo said, adding that it would be returned to the railway company and the smuggled objects would be examined by scientists.
The passengers from the affected wagon were moved to other carriages and the train continued from the checkpoint at Terespol on the Belarus border to its destination, Warsaw.

The television report said the level of radiation coming from the cross, about 40 milligrays an hour, was within the accepted annual maximum limit for humans but was the highest ever registered for any object at the Terespol border.
The report did not say how the cross came to be radioactive.
Polish border crossings have equipment for checking vehicles and trains to prevent the smuggling of radioactive materials.
Customs officials also regularly confiscate antique Russian Orthodox icons and devotional objects being smuggled for sale in the West.
